Section 5 · Coordination · Plate 38

The Dispatcher

You know the work needs doing, but not who should do it. Dispatch turns that uncertainty into a visible route: an existing teammate, the memories they need, a fresh work session, and a reason recorded on the task.

verified against the live command catalog and graph rules on 2026-08-20

Choosing a teammate is judgment. A bad route often looks fine at first: a session starts, a status turns green, and the mismatch stays hidden until the work fails. The Dispatcher exists to make that choice with more context—and leave the choice on the record.

01Watch one route form

Press Play route or step through it. The task title suggests invite-screen work; the memory graph reveals that session TTL and cookie policy are the real center of gravity.

01 · IntakeThe task is real; the right teammate is still a judgment call.

Still framesUse Step or the range control. Every route state remains available without animation.

1 / 7
  1. A task is handed to session dispatch.
  2. The server stores a message on the task and delivers trusted routing control to a Dispatcher session; the requester note remains untrusted material.
  3. Dispatcher reads the existing teammate roster.
  4. Dispatcher reads the memory graph for evidence of fit.
  5. Dispatcher chooses existing teammate Juniper and makes the task remember the two needed memories.
  6. Dispatcher spawns a new Juniper work session; working_on and server-recorded dispatched_by edges preserve the route.
  7. Dispatcher replies on the task thread with who it chose and why. Dispatcher never performs the task.

02The public command stays small

You provide the subject, not the teammate. If you already know who should work, use session spawn; choosing a teammate is the entire point of session dispatch.

The response reports the derived task, the Dispatcher session, delivery, and whether that Dispatcher session had to be started. The actual routing result arrives later as a threaded message on the task.

03What stays on the record

The route is more than a running terminal. It leaves graph evidence that another person—or the next agent—can inspect later.

The request survives delivery trouble.

The message is stored on the task before terminal delivery. An undelivered result is degraded, not erased.

The route has lineage.

The worker session points to the Dispatcher session with the server-recorded dispatched_by edge.

The judgment is readable.

Dispatcher replies on the request thread with the teammate, memories, and reason. Its rounded-square avatar marks teammate authorship structurally.

Honest boundary. Dispatch does not guarantee that a suitable teammate exists. Dispatcher must say so instead of creating a teammate, editing someone’s prompt or model, routing badly, or doing the task itself.
